subject: MSA addendum: license boundary & evidence access for private deployment
messages:
From: Matthew Jensen <matthew.jensen@asterhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
Cc: procurement@asterhealth.com
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MSA addendum for private deployment — license boundary & evidence access

Hi Karthik / Laura,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Attached is our first-pass redline of the MSA addendum for the private (on-prem/VPC) deployment. Main asks from our side:

- Clarify license scope so the runtime snapshot and model artifacts remain under Redwood license but customer has explicit limited-use rights for the deployed instance.
- Define the evidence access pathway: when AsterHealth requests a forensic snapshot or witness validation, describe the roles, timeline, and who can access the snapshot.
- Escrow-like request: we are asking for a short-form escrow or sealed-deposit option for the runtime image if Redwood ceases support for the tenancy. We understand full escrow is complex; we are open to alternatives (witnessed snapshot, third-party custodian).

Attached: Aster_MSA_Addendum_v1_redlines.pdf (redline) and a short workflow doc. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the evidence access workflow with limited operator access (timeboxed, read-only, recorded session)?

Next steps: if possible please route to your legal and infra teams — we aim to complete commercial negotiations by Sep 10 to align with procurement window.

Appreciate it,

Matthew Jensen
Director, Procurement
AsterHealth Systems
[Attachment: Aster_MSA_Addendum_v1_redlines.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: Proposed_Evidence_Access_Workflow.docx (docx)]
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com, david_kim@redwood.example.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.example.com
Cc: Matthew Jensen <matthew.jensen@asterhealth.com>, procurement <procurement@asterhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA addendum for private deployment — license boundary & evidence access

Laura / David / Naomi — looping you in per Matthew's attachments. High-level asks from Aster: limited runtime rights, a narrowly scoped evidence access process, and an escrow-like contingency for snapshot access.

Laura: can legal confirm whether we can: 1) state a non-exclusive, revocable runtime license for deployed artifacts; 2) accept a witnessed-snapshot alternative to full source-code escrow; and 3) propose a standard timeline for evidence requests (e.g., 10 business days notification + 3 business day access window for witness validation)?

David: operationally — would a read-only witnessed session (audit console access with live recording and a one-time snapshot export to a shared S3 presigned link) meet Aster's ask? What risks / telemetry retention policies would we need to document?

I will hold on marking changes back to Aster until we have alignment. Matthew — thanks for the clear redlines, we'll come back with proposed language and an operations playbook.

-Karthik
VP, Partnerships & BizDev
Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, david_kim@redwood.example.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.example.com
Cc: Matthew Jensen <matthew.jensen@asterhealth.com>, procurement <procurement@asterhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 13:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA addendum for private deployment — license boundary & evidence access

Karthik / team / Matthew — quick legal read and operational notes below. I kept my comments focused to limit friction on procurement timeline.

1) License scope: we can draft language that: (a) grants Aster a limited, non-transferable runtime license to use the deployed instance for its internal business purposes; (b) expressly reserves model IP and underlying binaries to Redwood; (c) permits Aster to create operational backups of their configuration and customer data but not the model artifacts. Suggested clause: "Customer may operate the Deployed Instance solely for Customer's internal business operations; Customer shall not reproduce, modify, or redistribute Model artifacts outside of the Deployed Instance."

2) Evidence access / witness option: we can accept a witnessed verification and a sealed snapshot deposit with a named third-party custodian as a fallback. Proposed controls:
- Request flow: Customer issues written request to Redwood legal@redwood.example.com with justification and attestation.
- Authorization: requests limited to two named customer approvers; Redwood will require a nondisclosure & limited-scope access addendum prior to any session.
- Timeline: Redwood will acknowledge within 5 business days; access must occur within 10 business days from acknowledgment; sessions limited to 2 hours unless mutually agreed.
- Recording & chain-of-custody: sessions will be recorded; snapshots will be checksum-signed and stored with a third-party custodian (we can propose IronGate Custody as an example).

3) Escrow-like fallback: full code escrow is not feasible for our model licensing; however, we can offer a sealed runtime image deposit with access conditions outlined above. We will supplement with an SLA carveout describing support obligations for continued operation after Redwood termination.

4) Attachments & redlines: I will prepare a clean addendum with tracked language and an operations annex showing the witness flow. That annex will include sample auth forms and a triage contact list.

Action items:
- David: confirm technical feasibility for the 2-hour witnessed session + presigned snapshot export and identify retention/telemetry side effects.
- Naomi: prepare a one-page checklist for the NDLA (nondisclosure + limited access) we will ask Aster to sign.
- Karthik: can you propose the named third-party custodian(s) Aster would accept?

I will aim to have the first cleaned addendum by EOD tomorrow to keep the Sep 10 procurement window realistic.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Legal_annotated_addendum_outline.docx (docx) — will upload soon]
From: Matthew Jensen <matthew.jensen@asterhealth.com>

Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA addendum for private deployment — license boundary & evidence access

Laura / Karthik — this is great, appreciate the pragmatic approach. Three quick confirmations: 

1) Aster is comfortable with a sealed runtime-image deposit + named third-party custodian (we prefer neutral custodians; I'll put forward two names this afternoon).
2) The proposed timelines (ack 5 BD / access within 10 BD) are acceptable. The 2-hour witnessed window is fine as long as we can request a secondary session within 30 days if needed.
3) Procurement would like a single-sheet summary of the evidence access workflow and the NDLA checklist to attach to the PO.

If you can send the cleaned addendum and the one-sheet / checklist, procurement will begin internal approvals and we can aim for signatures the week of Sep 6. We will want to complete DocuSign for the MSA addendum + Order Form simultaneously — can Redwood generate the DocuSign envelope when the addendum is final?

Thanks — will share custodian names shortly.

Matthew
Director, Procurement
AsterHealth Systems
